- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.31) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate next period’s forecast by 10–15% to correct for overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 periods, apply a 2–3% upward bias adjustment for the next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.67) and forecast deviates > 3% from true, align forecast to 3-period moving average of true values.  
- For horizon > 10 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is weak or volatile, to account for mean reversion.
